messages:
Maya (Design): Heads-up — quick design review request: invite panel feels cramped when roles matrix is expanded. can we discuss layout + keyboard focus?
Chris (PM): +1. Saw a few customer tickets about confused SSO toggle placement too.
Anna (UX): I prototyped two options: 1) compact roles overlay, 2) collapsible roles rows. sharing Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/invite-panel-v2
design-bot: New Figma link posted by Anna: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/invite-panel-v2 (viewers: @product)
Tom (Frontend): Quick note — collapsible rows are doable but will need animation tweaks to avoid layout shift during focus. also, we need aria-expanded states.
Priya (Accessibility): Important: when expanding roles, keyboard focus must remain on the expanded row header or the first checkbox — otherwise screen reader users lose context. Also the SSO toggle should have an accessible label: `labelledby` isn't enough if it's visually separated.
Maya (Design): Good call. Proposal: move SSO toggle up, next to "Invite settings" heading, add explanatory microcopy, and provide a tooltip. That reduces scanning.
Chris (PM): If we move the toggle, can we keep audit-log link visible? customers often want quick link to see invite events (who invited, SSO changes).
Anna (UX): Idea: add a persistent "Audit" icon in the panel header — small link that opens the audit drawer. It won't compete with invite actions.
Jin (Support): +1 from support. A recent case: customer couldn't find why SSO invites failed. they kept looking in org settings and missed the audit entry. If Audit is 1 click from invite panel that's helpful.
Tom (Frontend): Implementation note: header icon can be a button with `aria-controls` to open the audit drawer. we should ensure focus returns to the invite panel when the drawer closes.
Priya (Accessibility): Also: color contrast for the compact roles badges is too low on dark theme. need >= 4.5:1 for text on badge.
Maya (Design): I'll update the mock to increase contrast and show keyboard focus rings. Also adding clearer copy: change "SSO invites" -> "Require SSO for this invite". Thoughts?
Chris (PM): That copy is clearer. But let's keep the help tooltip with details: "Enforce SSO for this invite — if enabled, users must sign in via your organization's SSO."
Anna (UX): Another micro tweak: inline error copy when email domain rejects should be explicit: "This domain is blocked by org policy" instead of generic "Invite failed."
Tom (Frontend): For keyboard nav, propose `tabindex=0` on row headers and move checkboxes into natural tab order. Also expose a keyboard shortcut: `I` to open invite panel from org settings (optional).
Priya (Accessibility): Shortcut is fine if discoverable — add it to the panel header tooltip and the keyboard shortcuts list. Ensure it can be disabled via settings.
Maya (Design): Ok next steps: I'll push updated Figma with 3 key frames (collapsed, expanded, audit drawer open) by EOD. @Tom can you estimate dev effort after that?
Tom (Frontend): Quick estimate: 2-3 dev days for the UI + 1 day to hook audit drawer + QA for keyboard/screen reader. More if we add fancy animations.
Chris (PM): Good. Let's target an A/B internal rollout behind a feature flag. we'll measure invite completion rate and support ticket reduction.
Jin (Support): Please add a short changelog blurb for the support docs once design is settled.
Maya (Design): Will do. tagging this thread in the design review doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/invite-panel-review
Anna (UX): Will add accessibility checklist to the review doc (focus order, aria labels, contrast swatches).
Priya (Accessibility): I'll run a quick NVDA/VoiceOver pass once components are ready.
Chris (PM): Thanks all. Quick follow-up: @Maya can you include the updated error states and the audit drawer copy in the Figma? then we'll schedule a 30m review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Maya (Design): Yep — on it. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
